Construct continuous patient histories

getTrajectoriesContinuous.Rd

This function returns selected state intervals with trajectory boundary markers.

Usage

getTrajectoriesContinuous(
  cdm,
  patientData,
  stateSelection,
  statePriorityVector,
  absorbingStates = NULL,
  studyName = "",
  addPersonalData = TRUE,
  allowedStatesList = list(),
  stateLevels = NULL,
  outOfCohortAllowed = FALSE
)

Arguments

cdm

a cdm object

patientData

Object of class data.frame with columns subject_id, state_label, STATE_START_DATE, STATE_END_DATE

stateSelection

Selection of the type of ordering

statePriorityVector

All states in prioritized order

absorbingStates

Absorbing states in dataframe

studyName

name chosen for study, is used as a folder name

addPersonalData

Logical, indicating whether or not to add personal data for each patient

allowedStatesList

A list object which indicates accessible states from said state

stateLevels

Ordered study-wide state labels used to assign stable IDs.

outOfCohortAllowed

Whether retained states may extend the target endpoint.

Value

A dataframe of selected intervals and boundary markers. Models that require unique timestamps need an explicit rule for simultaneous records.

Details

Target intervals supply START and EXIT boundaries even without state records. Selected intervals retain their endpoints and simultaneous records retain equal elapsed times. Gaps do not imply continued clinical state membership. Absorbing states end the trajectory at their retained endpoint. Earlier overlapping intervals are capped at that endpoint so that no clinical interval extends beyond the shortened follow-up. Priority selection assigns shared days to the higher-priority state and retains only non-empty fragments of lower-priority intervals. Only transition-eligible states compete for priority. Continuing a selected interval does not require a self-transition when another record starts or ends. A selected absorbing interval retains its bounded recorded endpoint. Every clinical state in the bounded input must appear in statePriorityVector. Missing states raise an error rather than being silently discarded. Transition rules are checked before the absorbing-state cutoff. Empty rules mean unrestricted transitions. Rejected records do not change the last retained state, and only a retained absorbing record can end the trajectory.
